stories.headline: Trump's 'Op Economic Outcast' against Iran: What sanctions threat could mean for India
stories.title: Trump's 'Op Economic Outcast' against Iran: What sanctions threat could mean for India
stories.summary: The Donald Trump administration said on Monday that the new US sanctions are intended to shut off every potential source of revenue for Iran, while warning other countries that continuing their economic ties with Tehran could expose them to retaliation.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Launching an ‘economic onslaught’ on Iran, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that President Donald Trump is making phone calls to world leaders with specific requests to stop all interactions with Iran.
The move comes amid the ongoing US-Iran conflict which has shaken the world economy and global oil markets since the end of February this year.

Bessent said Monday that the new US sanctions are intended to shut off every potential source of revenue for Iran, while warning other countries that continuing their economic ties with Tehran could expose them to retaliation.
He said it was “no longer acceptable to operate in the gray spaces” of the conflict.
The US has imposed sanctions on Iran for decades.
These measures prevent designated entities from accessing the dollar-based financial system.
Iran, however, has managed to evade the restrictions by quickly setting up new front companies and other entities, as well as registering vessels under new arrangements.
“Iran now faces a very clear choice, with only two paths before them: complete global isolation and a subsistence economy, or a path back to normalcy with an opportunity to rejoin the global economy.
Today, we are launching Operation Economic Outcast to foreclose every other option available to the Iranian regime,” Bessent said.
“Beginning today, the actions of the Treasury and other agencies will tighten the noose and block every potential source of revenue that funds the IRGC and the evil Iranian regime.
We are enforcing a zero leakage approach.
There will be no minimal breathing space for the regime to rebuild its capacity to inflict terror against America and the world,” he added.

stories.headline: Amit Shah calls for AI-driven analysis of intelligence data to counter national-security challenges
stories.title: Amit Shah calls for AI-driven analysis of intelligence data to counter national-security challenges
stories.summary: New Delhi, Aug 24: Directing security agencies to strictly deal with infiltration, Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Monday called for an artificial intelligence-driven analysis of intelligence data to counter various national-security challenges. Inaugurating the two-day ninth National Security Strategies (NSS) Conference-2026, Shah also laid emphasis on training for the implementation of the anti-terror policy developed by his ministry called the "PRAHAAR" scheme, according to a government statement. The home minister also asked the agencies to expedite trial by bringing back fugitives, using trial-in-absentia provisions and undertaking a comprehensive and integrated approach while investigating anti-terror cases under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), the statement said. "The Home Minister directed that an AI-based analysis of information available on MAC (Multi Agency Centre) platforms should be done to create SOPs to counter various national security challenges. Union Home Minister directed all the agencies to take strict measures against infiltration," it added. The conference, being held in a hybrid mode, is being attended by 850 senior security and police officers from across the country, besides Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Intelligence Bureau Director Mahesh Dixit, Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) Director Praveen Sood and Secretary of the Research and Analysis Wing (RAW) Parag Jain, among others. Several security officials and domain experts, deputy national security advisors, heads of paramilitary forces and directors general of police (DGPs) of state police forces are also participating in the conference, the statement said. "On the first day of the conference, discussions focussed on critical aspects of national security, including response to counter-terrorism challenges, fusion, analysis and operationalisation of intelligence through the Multi Agency Centre (MAC), vision document on narcotics control, detection and deportation of illegal migrants, a policy framework to combat cyber-crime and proxy warfare by Pakistan," it said. Before inaugurating the conference, Shah laid a wreath at the Martyrs' Column in remembrance of the Intelligence Bureau personnel who died in the line of duty while safeguarding national security and integrity. The deliberations on the second day will continue on threats from sub-aerial systems and countermeasures, securing the blue economy, information warfare and its implications for national security, and the need for a bio-security framework. Pursuant to the directions of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the NSSC is being held in a hybrid format every year since 2021. The objective of the conference is finding solutions to major national-security challenges, using the extensive experience of officers working at the grassroots level in collaboration with domain experts.

stories.headline: PDF blames successive govts for J&K hydropower sellout
stories.title: PDF blames successive govts for J&K hydropower sellout
stories.summary: Srinagar, Aug 24: President of the People’s Democratic Front (PDF) and former Cabinet Minister Hakeem Mohammad Yaseen on Monday strongly opposed the recently approved hike in electricity tariffs in Jammu and Kashmir, demanding its immediate withdrawal and asking the government to honour its electoral commitment of providing 200 units of free electricity. In a statement, Yaseen said the hike would further burden ordinary consumers already facing economic difficulties, unemployment and rising household expenses. Yaseen said successive political parties, including the ruling Jammu and Kashmir National Conference (JKNC), must share responsibility for what he described as the failure to secure adequate benefits for the people of J&K from the region's water and hydropower resources. “Jammu and Kashmir was blessed by nature with abundant water resources, yet our people continue to face power shortages and are now being asked to pay more for electricity. Successive governments have been in power, but no serious decision was taken to ensure that the people of J&K receive the rightful benefit from their own resources,” he said. The PDF president alleged that political parties that have governed J&K over the years failed to protect the economic interests of the common people while allowing the region's hydropower potential to be utilised for projects benefiting the Centre. “We are a resource-rich region, but our own people are being made to purchase electricity at higher rates. Those responsible for this situation should apologise to the people,” Yaseen said. He also questioned the timing of the tariff revision, saying that the government should have taken into account the economic hardships faced by households, particularly amid unemployment and other pressing socioeconomic challenges. Yaseen urged Chief Minister Omar Abdullah to intervene and direct the concerned authorities to withdraw the tariff hike.
